subject: Performance SLO - private VPC network qualification / next steps
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC perf SLOs (thanks for the call)

Hi Marissa / Jordan -

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Appreciate the quick demo and the outline of Redwood's private VPC options. On the call we committed to share more specifics on our latency targets and the network path details you asked for.

For context: our critical realtime path is the ingestion pipeline that calls LLM endpoints for fraud-scoring. We need 95th percentile inference latency <= 120ms (end-to-end), sustained throughput ~250 req/s with bursts to 500 req/s, and streaming responses for multi-step scoring (chunked output acceptable).

Per your ask, I'm attaching a short network capture from our staging cluster and a diagram of our peering topology. Let me know if these are the right artifacts.

Attachments: network_trace_acme.pcap (15MB), acme_peering_diagram.png

Next steps: can you confirm what internal latency budget Redwood would expect for a private VPC/on-prem deployment (network hop budgets + processing), and whether you can meet 95p <= 120ms at the numbers above?

Thanks - Alex
Alex Torres
Platform Engineering, Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC perf SLOs (thanks for the call)

Alex -

Great summary, and thanks for the attachments. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps:

1) Recap of SLO asks (as we understand):
- 95p end-to-end inference <= 120ms
- steady-state throughput ~250 req/s, bursts to 500 req/s
- support streaming responses (server push/chunked)

2) What we'll validate from Redwood:
- baseline per-token processing latency for the model variant you plan to use (we'll run perf tests against our private runtime)
- expected added latency for the VPC egress/peering path and recommended network config (VPN vs peering)
- concurrency behavior and recommended autoscale settings for Dedicated pools in a Private deployment
- streaming performance and how we surface chunked tracing/KB cache effects in the SLOs

3) Immediate ask from you: confirm the model size/variant you'll want to pin for production and a sample payload size (tokens) so we can run realistic load tests.

I've looped in Jordan and David to handle the detailed network/throughput questions below. Proposed schedule: our infra team will run an initial perf run Wednesday (2028-04-12) and share results + recommended config by EOD Thursday. Does that work for your team?

Best -
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC perf SLOs (thanks for the call)

Alex - thanks for the pcap and topology diagram. A few technical clarifications that will affect our internal latency budget:

- What is the typical MTU and whether you have jumbo frames enabled between your staging cluster and the peering/VPN endpoint?
- Are you terminating TLS at the edge (load balancer) or at the application host? Redwood's ideal path minimises TLS TPS at the model gateway to reduce CPU queuing.
- Do you plan to use AWS Transit Gateway/VPC peering/direct connect or a site-to-site VPN? Peering/direct-connect typically gives us ~3-8ms extra RTT depending on region; VPNs can add 10-40ms depending on throughput and encryption.
- For bursting to 500 req/s, do you have a request queue or backpressure expectation on your side (we can advise on queueing/backoff policies to avoid head-of-line effects).

If you can share sample request size (payload tokens) and whether you need server-sent-events style streaming or a websocket proxy, that will let us size concurrency and expected KV-cache hit behaviors.

Technical note: for Private/VPC we typically budget ~40-60ms for model inference on a 16GB-quantized variant at 1-2 token response sizes; network budget is set to meet the 95p target remaining. We'll validate this precisely with your payloads.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@netconnect.io>
Date: 2028-04-10T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC perf SLOs (thanks for the call)

Jordan / Marissa -

Answers inline:
- MTU: 9001 (jumbo frames enabled)
- TLS termination: we terminate TLS at the ALB, and traffic to hosts is mTLS within the VPC
- Connectivity: currently using AWS Transit Gateway with a DirectConnect link; plan is to use VPC peering between our transit VPC and Redwood's VPC endpoint if that simplifies routing.
- Burst handling: we have a local in-memory request queue with a 2s max wait; we can adjust backoff if needed.

Sample payload: avg request ~420 tokens (50 token prompt + 370 token context), typical response size ~40 tokens. Streaming: SSE acceptable; websocket not required.

I attached the pcap you requested (network_trace_acme.pcap) and our minimal topology PDF. Happy to jump on a short tech call if you want to walk the trace.

Regards -
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Sam Park <sam.park@netconnect.io>
Date: 2028-04-10T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC perf SLOs (thanks for the call)

Perfect - thanks for the detail, Alex. Action items and next steps from Redwood:

- Jordan/David: run targeted perf tests on 16GB quantized variant using the provided payload (420 tokens in / 40 tokens out), and report 50p/95p/99p latencies under steady 250 req/s and burst 500 req/s. Please include streaming test with SSE. (ETA: 2028-04-12 EOD)
- Marissa: I'll send a concise mutual action plan and an updated SOW draft (capacity and expected config) after we have test results.
- Alex/Sam: please confirm if VPC peering is acceptable; if so we'll generate instructions for routing and security groups.

I've attached our private deployment perf spec for reference: redwood_private_specs.pdf

If we validate that 95p <= 120ms under the stated topology, we'll include the SLO in the draft and propose a dedicated private pool with autoscale headroom. If we see a gap, we'll propose mitigations (edge caching, reduced quantization tradeoffs, or regional proxying).

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday 2028-04-13 10:00am PT to review results?

Thanks -
Marissa
